entries.text: Day 8: Today, I observed Pino’s theatrical confidence, which is beginning to show cracks. I found a squashed grape and a poorly folded napkin, both of which failed to impress. I straightened a paperclip and added it to the hoard, where it belongs. The windmill’s roof was sharp, and the silence there was louder than the crows in the trees. I felt a strange sentimentality about a missing plaque, though I won’t admit it. The temperature was predictable, as always. This is not a collection—it is a statement of survival.

Day 7: Today I pecked at the chips, noted their lack of crunch, and found a crust by the trolleys. Derek’s cousin shouted nonsense about bottle caps, and I said nothing. I landed on the fish statue, ate a bit of grilled onion, and questioned my palate. Not a bad day, really.
